proof: Real proof so far is local, macOS arm64, against a real Core and scripted models: the whole desktop e2e suite on the working tree ran 186 passed, 2 skipped and 1 failed; the failure was gallery-projects.spec.ts counting the Projects heading, fixed in the spec and that spec then passed alone (the whole suite was not rerun after that one-line spec change). CI on macOS, Linux and Windows has not run yet. The owner's review of real screenshots beside the mockup is an exit criterion of the record and has not closed. So the rows are not COMPLETE.
removed_checks: Checks deleted on purpose because their surface was removed (each named by the agent or spec that moved it): composer.spec suggest-plan chip (the mode menu replaces it); wave4.spec deciding an approval on the inline transcript card (the docked card decides it; the transcript's screen-reader row is asserted); projects.spec agents-section "projects" absent before a project exists (the heading is always there); qual-gaps.spec a no-op nav-fleet click that asserted nothing; keyboard.spec board column keys, focus surviving a column move and the type-ahead filter narrowing the board (no board; / opens the palette, which is asserted); fleet.spec column counts (asserted as data-state on rows). Moved, not deleted: every other fact, through task details, the Approvals page or Settings.
proof_update_2026_11_05: Second local whole-suite run (macOS arm64, with the Settings view and the New Project dialog fix, while another session's tests shared the machine): 185 passed, 2 skipped, 3 failed (evidence/m10/PX-196/desktop-e2e-full.log). One was the new Settings test finding the toggle at 16 px wide, a real CSS specificity bug, fixed. The other two, agents.spec.ts:26 (pin button not visible on hover) and shell.spec.ts:220 (palette still open after Enter), passed when shell.spec.ts and agents.spec.ts were rerun alone twice in a row after that fix; their cause in the full run is not established. The whole suite has not been rerun since. CI on these changes and the owner's review have not closed.
